body.p: This listing of claims is responsive to the Office Action mailed November 12, 2024, which has been carefully considered. Reconsideration and allowance of the subject application are requested for at least the following reasons.

Applicant greatly appreciates the remarks on page 11 of the Office Action indicating that claim 2 is objected to as being dependent upon a rejected base claim but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the limitations of the base claim and any intervening claims.

Claims 14-15 and 21 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention.

Applicant has amended claim 14 to provide proper antecedent basis. Applicant notes that the amendment to claim 14 also addresses the rejection of claim 15. Applicant has also amended claim 21 to depend from independent claim 19.
Reconsideration and withdrawal of the above rejections under 35 U.S.C. § 112 is therefore respectfully requested.

Claims 1, 3, 5-8, and 19 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over Mannheimer et al. (USPN 8,352,004, hereinafter "Mannheimer") in view of Tjin (USPGPUB 2004/0074307, hereinafter "Tjin") and evidenced by Bartol et al. (USPGPUB 2014/0058288, hereinafter "Bartol"). Claims 11, 14-15, 17, and 22-23 were rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over the combination of Mannheimer and Tjin in further in view of Besko et al. (USPGPUB 2010/0249557, hereinafter "Besko"). Claims 21 and 25 were rejected under 35

U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over the combination of Mannheimer and Tjin in further in view of Tverskoy (USPGPUB 2013/0218025, hereinafter "Tverskoy"). Claim 18 was rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as being unpatentable over the combination of Mannheimer, Tjin, and Besko in further in view of Tverskoy.

While Applicant respectfully disagrees with the above rejections, Applicant has amended independent claims 1 and 19 based on the allowable subject matter of claim 2 in order to facilitate advancement of the instant application to allowance. Applicant respectfully requests entry of the instant amendment under 37 C.F.R. § 1.116. No further search or consideration is believed to be necessary. Nothing in this amendment should be considered an explicit or implicit acquiescence of any of the above rejections or an explicit or implicit dedication of subjection matter. Applicant expressly reserves the right to file one or more continuation applications directed to disclosed and unclaimed subject matter.

It is believed that all the pending claims have been addressed. However, the absence of a reply to a specific rejection, issue or comment does not signify agreement with or concession of that rejection, issue or comment. In addition, because the arguments made above may not be exhaustive, there may be reasons for patentability of any or all pending claims (or other claims) that have not been expressed. Finally, nothing in this paper should be construed as intent to concede any issue regarding any claim, except as specifically stated in this paper.

Having dealt with all the objections raised by the Examiner, it is respectfully submitted that the present application, as amended, is in condition for allowance. Thus, early allowance is earnestly solicited.
If the Examiner desires personal contact for further disposition of this case, the Examiner is invited to call the undersigned Attorney at 603.668.6560.
In the event there are any fees due, please charge them to our Deposit Account No. 50- 2121.
Paul J. Kroon, Jr. Reg. No. 51,902
